exposure: Implementation of strategies to improve compliance with evidence-based criteria for correct positioning and attachment
outcome: Compliance with evidence-based criteria for correct positioning and attachment in breastfeeding infants
Rates of compliance for maternal criteria (guidance to women, breastfeeding support, encouragement from families)
cohort: The study included 87 mothers and 20 midwives in the baseline audit, and 93 mothers and 17 midwives in the follow-up audit, focusing on breastfeeding infants delivered by cesarean section at La Fe University and Polytechnical Hospital.
finding: The implementation project significantly improved compliance with evidence-based criteria for promoting correct positioning and attachment during breastfeeding in women who had given birth by cesarean section, with maternal criteria compliance increasing by 42-51% and professional training reaching 100% compliance.
mod_finding: The implemented strategies were specifically designed and found to be effective in improving breastfeeding support and compliance with related criteria for mothers who had given birth by cesarean section.
followup_time: During postpartum hospitalization (specific duration not mentioned)
